title: The Early Bird Catches the Leak: Unveiling Timing Side Channels in LLM Serving Systems
venue: arXiv 2409.20002; arXiv comment says accepted by IEEE TIFS
quote: a set of new timing side channels in LLM systems
proves: Black-box co-tenant TTFT timing detects KV-cache and semantic-cache hits; token-by-token search recovers system prompts and peer users' prompts; leaks seen in SGLang, GPTCache and online services. Uses eviction only as a noise-clearing tool (batches of irrelevant requests evict the cache). Mitigation: share prefixes only in K-token units; PII anonymization for semantic cache.
does_not_prove: Eviction is used to reset state, not as the leaked signal; no LRU-targeted eviction probing of victim entries. No KV compression/eviction-policy (H2O, SnapKV) leakage. No resource-exhaustion study.
bearing: prefix-cache timing leak; semantic-cache leak; eviction as attack tool; defense (K-token sharing)

title: I Know What You Asked: Prompt Leakage via KV-Cache Sharing in Multi-Tenant LLM Serving
quote: allowing unauthorized reconstruction of user prompts and compromising sensitive user information
proves: PROMPTPEEK: ordinary-user adversary on SGLang reconstructs other users' prompts; signal is response ORDER under Longest Prefix Match scheduling. PDF (also opened) shows LRU eviction used in two auxiliary ways: inferring victim eviction from eviction of the attacker's own later candidates, and flushing the cache by saturating GPU memory with dummy requests.
does_not_prove: Leak signal is LPM scheduling order, not eviction itself; eviction is inferred only to time prompt switching. No compression-policy leakage, no attack that reads victim content from what was evicted, no resource-exhaustion goal.
bearing: prefix-cache scheduling side channel; LRU eviction as auxiliary signal; cache flush by memory saturation

title: Auditing Prompt Caching in Language Model APIs
quote: We detect global cache sharing across users in seven API providers, including OpenAI
proves: Statistical hypothesis-test audits on TTFT detect prompt caching and cross-user global cache sharing in real commercial APIs; timing also leaked architecture (OpenAI embedding model is decoder-only).
does_not_prove: Detection/audit only, not full prompt extraction. No eviction-driven or compression-driven leakage; no resource exhaustion.
bearing: prefix-cache timing leak; commercial API audit; cross-tenant sharing; High: the only documented production disclosure wave found; precedent and method for responsible disclosure.; exploiter: strongest evidence that cross-tenant cache timing was a real, deployed exposure

title: InputSnatch: Stealing Input in LLM Services via Timing Side-Channel Attacks
venue: arXiv 2411.18191 (preprint; a Springer chapter with similar title exists but was not opened)
quote: conduct experiments across two cache mechanisms
proves: Black-box timing attack: ML/LLM-guided input constructor plus statistical time analyzer detects cache hits to steal user inputs; evaluated on two cache mechanisms (prefix and semantic per secondary reports).
does_not_prove: Abstract page does not name cache mechanisms or discuss eviction. No compression-policy or resource-exhaustion study.
bearing: prefix-cache and semantic-cache timing leak

title: Selective KV-Cache Sharing to Mitigate Timing Side-Channels in LLM Inference
quote: a unified radix-tree-based memory manager with path compression and sensitivity-aware eviction
proves: SafeKV defense: detects sensitive KV blocks and isolates them from cross-tenant reuse; RDR safeguard bounds residual leakage; TTFT overhead vs full isolation cut up to 40.58%, throughput up to 2.66x.
does_not_prove: Eviction is part of the defense, not analyzed as a leak channel; does not evaluate attacks that exploit its own sensitivity-aware eviction or memory pressure. No KV compression leakage; no resource exhaustion against the detector.
bearing: defense; selective sharing; sensitivity-aware eviction

title: CachePrune: Privacy-Aware and Fine-Grained KV Cache Sharing for Efficient LLM Inference
quote: Existing defenses disable sharing entirely to prevent leakage
proves: Token-level privacy-aware KV reuse on vLLM by the PromptPeek group; claims to eliminate direct leakage via the reuse side channel with 4.5x lower TTFT and 44% higher hit rate vs SOTA defenses.
does_not_prove: Threat model is direct reuse probing; abstract does not address eviction-driven or memory-occupancy leakage, compression, or exhaustion.
bearing: defense; selective sharing

title: PrefixWall: Mitigating Prefix Caching Side Channels in Shared LLM Systems
quote: cache hits are faster than misses, creating observable latency differences.
proves: Monitoring defense for APC: tracks cross-user reuse, flags suspicious sharing, isolates only affected prefixes; up to 70% higher reuse and 30% lower latency vs user isolation.
does_not_prove: Abstract covers hit/miss probing only; no eviction-driven channel, no compression, no adaptive attacker evading the monitor or exhausting it.
bearing: defense; prefix-cache timing leak; anomaly detection

title: Governing the KV Cache: Preventing Timing Side-Channel Leakage in Multi-Tenant LLM Inference
quote: an adversarial tenant can reconstruct another tenant's private prompt by probing cache-hit latency
proves: KVGov: HMAC per-principal salt makes cache keys disjoint (ablation: salt necessary and sufficient); timing channel measured on vLLM 0.26.0 A100 and Apple Metal (cold/cached TTFT ratio 0.22).
does_not_prove: Defense evaluated only in simulation. Salting blocks hit-probing but per-principal salt does not isolate shared eviction/capacity, so eviction or occupancy channels are not addressed; page does not mention eviction.
bearing: defense; cache salting; prefix-cache timing leak

title: Characterizing Contention-Induced Reliability Collapse in KV-Cache Timing Side Channels for Multi-Tenant LLM Serving
quote: mean Cohen's d drops from 0.7789 with no synthetic workers to 0.2109 with two workers
proves: Measures prefix-cache timing attack reliability on live vLLM and SGLang under load; reliability collapses with concurrency, so quiet-system results overestimate real-world threat.
does_not_prove: Abstract does not mention eviction; does not study eviction-based or memory-pressure channels (which might strengthen, not weaken, under load). No compression or exhaustion.
bearing: prefix-cache timing leak; realism/noise

title: Agent-Assisted Side-Channel Attacks on Non-Prefix KV Cache in RAG
quote: SpliceLeak executes a systematic two-phase privacy breach
proves: SpliceLeak: timing leak in chunk-aware fusion of non-prefix KV chunks (vLLM + LMCache) recovers hidden prompt length then tokens; up to 100% extraction in bounded-entropy settings; SpliceDefense (quantized chunk padding, constant-time boundary fusion).
does_not_prove: Non-prefix reuse/fusion timing only; abstract does not mention eviction or KV compression; no offload-tier eviction channel or exhaustion.
bearing: non-prefix KV reuse timing leak; RAG; defense

title: OptiLeak: Efficient Prompt Reconstruction via Reinforcement Learning in Multi-tenant LLM Services
quote: Multi-tenant LLM serving frameworks widely adopt shared Key-Value caches to enhance efficiency.
proves: RL/DPO-guided candidate generation cuts requests per token up to 12.48x for shared-KV prompt reconstruction on medical/financial benchmarks; argues cache leakage is underestimated.
does_not_prove: Improves search efficiency over existing oracles; abstract does not state the observed signal or any eviction use. No compression, no exhaustion.
bearing: prefix-cache leak; attack efficiency

title: When Speculation Spills Secrets: Side Channels via Speculative Decoding In LLMs
quote: we reveal a new side-channel whereby input-dependent patterns of correct and incorrect speculations
proves: Per-iteration token counts / packet sizes under speculative decoding (REST, LADE, BiLD, EAGLE) fingerprint queries (>75% of 50 prompts at T=0.3) and leak datastore contents; mitigations: padding, token aggregation.
does_not_prove: Network/output-observer channel; not KV cache sharing, eviction, or compression; no resource exhaustion.
bearing: speculative decoding side channel

title: Wiretapping LLMs: Network Side-Channel Attacks on Interactive LLM Services
quote: Network adversaries can leverage these side channels to learn sensitive information
proves: Indistinguishability framework plus attack on encrypted packet timing/size from speculative decoding and other optimizations; 71-92% private-attribute accuracy on vLLM, 50-90% on ChatGPT.
does_not_prove: Passive network observer; no co-tenant cache probing, no eviction or compression channels.
bearing: speculative decoding; network timing/size side channel

title: Remote Timing Attacks on Efficient Language Model Inference
quote: But these techniques introduce data-dependent timing characteristics.
proves: Encrypted-traffic timing from speculative sampling / parallel decoding infers topics (>90% precision on open systems), distinguishes messages on ChatGPT and Claude; active boosting attack recovers PII.
does_not_prove: Not about KV cache sharing, eviction, or compression; no exhaustion.
bearing: efficiency-optimization timing side channel

title: Whisper Leak: a side-channel attack on Large Language Models
quote: metadata patterns leak sufficient information to enable topic classification.
proves: Network observer classifies prompt topic from streaming packet size/timing across 28 LLMs (often >98% AUPRC); padding, batching, packet injection reduce but do not eliminate.
does_not_prove: Network metadata only; no KV cache, eviction, or compression mechanism.
bearing: streaming metadata side channel; defense evaluation

title: Stealing User Prompts from Mixture of Experts
quote: an adversary that can arrange for their queries to appear in the same batch of examples as a victim's queries
proves: Expert-Choice Routing capacity overflow plus torch.topk tie-breaking leaks victim tokens to a co-batched attacker; full prompt extracted on 2-layer Mixtral with O(VM^2) queries.
does_not_prove: Batch-co-location and capacity-overflow channel; not KV cache or eviction; toy model, authors judge real deployment infeasible today.
bearing: MoE routing side channel; batching

title: MoEcho: Exploiting Side-Channel Attacks to Compromise User Privacy in Mixture-of-Experts LLMs
quote: These input-dependent activation patterns leave distinctive temporal and spatial traces in hardware execution
proves: Four hardware channels (CPU cache occupancy, Pageout+Reload; GPU perf counters, TLB Evict+Reload) reveal MoE expert routing, enabling prompt inference and response reconstruction.
does_not_prove: Microarchitectural co-located attacker; not serving-level KV cache sharing or KV eviction policy; no exhaustion.
bearing: MoE routing side channel; hardware cache/TLB eviction

title: Spill The Beans: Exploiting CPU Cache Side-Channels to Leak Tokens from Large Language Models
quote: By co-locating an attack process on the same hardware as the victim model
proves: Flush+Reload on embedding vectors in shared CPU cache leaks generated tokens (80-90% of a high-entropy API key single-shot, ~40% of English text).
does_not_prove: Hardware-cache eviction, not KV-cache block eviction; co-located process; no serving-level compression or exhaustion.
bearing: CPU cache side channel; token leakage

title: Detokenization Leaks: Reconstructing Local LLM Outputs From Cache Traces
quote: our approach targets the detokenizer, a component used in default LLM inference pipelines.
proves: Flush+Reload on tokenizer code plus Prime+Probe recover locally hosted LLM outputs, including agent frameworks.
does_not_prove: Local co-resident CPU attacker; not KV cache sharing, KV eviction, or compression.
bearing: CPU cache side channel; detokenizer

title: Shadow in the Cache: Unveiling and Mitigating Privacy Risks of KV-cache in LLM Inference
quote: an attacker can reconstruct sensitive user inputs directly from the KV-cache
proves: Attacker with access to KV tensors reconstructs inputs via inversion, collision, and injection attacks; KV-Cloak obfuscation defense with low overhead.
does_not_prove: Direct KV access threat model, not a timing/eviction side channel; no compression-policy leakage; no exhaustion.
bearing: KV cache inversion; defense (obfuscation)

title: The Pitfalls of KV Cache Compression
quote: empirically demonstrating the impact of compression on leakage and general instruction-following.
proves: Under StreamingLLM, SnapKV, TOVA, H2O, K-Norm, some instructions are ignored and system prompt leakage rises; KV eviction bias is a contributing factor; proposes eviction-policy changes.
does_not_prove: Leakage is via model outputs (instructions dropped), not a timing/occupancy side channel; no adversarial manipulation of compression to leak another tenant's data; no resource exhaustion.
bearing: KV compression/eviction-policy induced leakage (closest to compression-driven gap)

title: vLLM design doc: Automatic Prefix Caching
quote: This prevents timing-based attacks where an adversary could infer cached content by observing latency differences.
proves: vLLM ships opt-in per-request cache_salt injected into the first block hash to isolate prefix reuse by trust group; eviction is LRU over a free queue.
does_not_prove: Salting isolates hits but the block pool and LRU free queue remain shared, so eviction/occupancy interference across salts is not addressed; no compression.
bearing: defense (cache salting); LRU eviction mechanics

title: Structuring Applications to Secure the KV Cache
quote: This might be done passively or through active manipulation to prime or flush the cache.
proves: Vendor guidance acknowledges active prime/flush probing of KV cache; recommends per-session identifiers early in prompt, input limits, per-tenant cache isolation, enumeration monitoring.
does_not_prove: Guidance, no measured attack; no eviction-driven inference evaluation or compression analysis.
bearing: practitioner defense; prime/flush acknowledgement

title: Prompt caching (OpenAI API guide)
quote: Caches are not shared across organizations and cannot be reused across regional processing boundaries
proves: Commercial provider isolates prompt caches per organization; entries expire (e.g., 30 minutes after last use for newer models).
does_not_prove: Intra-organization sharing remains (multi-user apps under one org); says nothing about eviction or capacity contention as a channel.
bearing: defense (per-org isolation); provider practice

title: The Pitfalls of KV Cache Compression
quote: effectively causing them to be completely ignored by the LLM
proves: Under benign multi-instruction prompts (IFEval; StreamingLLM, SnapKV, TOVA, H2O, K-Norm on Llama3.1 8B, Qwen2.5 14B), compression degrades some instructions much faster than others; system prompt leakage is a case study; compression method, instruction order and eviction bias drive it; simple eviction-policy fixes help.
does_not_prove: No active adversary crafting inputs to target eviction (leakage arises from benign compression, though leakage is a security outcome). Measures accuracy/leakage only, not memory or resource impact. Single-request, no multi-tenant serving.
bearing: robustness: instruction loss and system-prompt leakage under eviction

title: When Efficiency Meets Safety: A Benchmark Security Analysis of KV Cache Compression in Large Language Models
quote: where aggressive merging in shallow layers triggers functional head collapse, amplifying attack success rates
proves: Systematic jailbreak study across four model families: compression gives accidental robustness to optimization- and encoding-based attacks but merging-based compression amplifies human-designed jailbreak ASR; proposes Safe-CAM per-head merging restoring 0% ASR.
does_not_prove: Adversary is a jailbreaker seeking harmful output, not one targeting memory or compression ratio. No memory/resource attack measured. No multi-tenant serving setting.
bearing: robustness: jailbreaks under compression; safety-aware merging

title: AnchorKV: Safety-Aware KV Cache Compression via Soft Penalty with a Refusal Anchor
quote: fail to defend against jailbreak attacks
proves: Claims existing compression either fails to defend against jailbreaks or degrades safety alignment under aggressive eviction; proposes drop-in retention-score penalty along harmful key-space directions (refusal anchor).
does_not_prove: Adversary is a jailbreaker, not a resource attacker; does not test attacks adapted to AnchorKV's anchor beyond what abstract states. Accuracy/safety only, no memory exhaustion. No multi-tenant serving.
bearing: hardening: safety-aware eviction

title: RobustKV: Defending Large Language Models against Jailbreak Attacks via KV Eviction
quote: selectively removing critical tokens of harmful queries from key-value (KV) caches
proves: Uses eviction as a defense: jailbreak prompts inflate attention on their own tokens, so evicting low-importance tokens strips the hidden harmful query; claims an effectiveness-evasiveness dilemma against adaptive attackers.
does_not_prove: Studies an adversary (jailbreaker, including adaptive) but eviction is the defense, not the target. No memory/resource measurement. No multi-tenant serving. Shows attackers can shape attention importance, which is the lever for eviction-targeting attacks.
bearing: adversary vs eviction scoring; eviction as defense

title: Taming the Fragility of KV Cache Eviction in LLM Inference (DefensiveKV)
quote: we argue that this underlying assumption is inherently fragile
proves: Mean-aggregated importance scoring relies on a stability assumption that fails in extreme cases; defensive (worst-case-bounding) aggregation in linear time, plus layer-wise budgets, cuts quality loss 2.3x/4.3x at 20% cache over strongest baseline on 18 datasets.
does_not_prove: Worst-case is over benign data, not an adversary crafting inputs. Measures generation quality at fixed budget, not memory under attack. No multi-tenant serving.
bearing: hardening: worst-case eviction aggregation

title: CriticalKV: Optimizing KV Cache Eviction from an Output Perturbation Perspective
quote: optimizes the worst-case output perturbation to identify critical entries
proves: Attention weights alone are insufficient for eviction; bounding worst-case output perturbation (using value states) roughly halves compression loss as a plug-in to existing eviction methods.
does_not_prove: Worst-case is analytic over outputs, not adversarial inputs. Accuracy only, no memory/resource attack. No multi-tenant serving.
bearing: hardening: worst-case scoring

title: Semantic Integrity Matters: Benchmarking and Preserving High-Density Reasoning in KV Cache Compression (KVFundaBench, ShotKV)
quote: reasoning tasks exhibit severe Task-Dependent Degradation under aggressive compression due to disrupted CoT links
proves: Retrieval survives compression while reasoning degrades sharply; proposes ShotKV treating few-shot examples as units. This is the arXiv entry for the work the brief calls "Can LLMs maintain fundamental abilities under KV cache compression" (old title not shown on page, so not confirmed).
does_not_prove: Benign benchmarks only, no adversary. Accuracy and latency only, no memory exhaustion. No multi-tenant serving.
bearing: robustness: task-dependent degradation

title: Rethinking Key-Value Cache Compression Techniques for Large Language Model Serving
quote: compressing KV cache may lead to longer outputs, resulting in increased end-to-end latency
proves: Serving-side evaluation of compression: compressed models can emit longer outputs, erasing throughput/latency gains; compression benefits are workload-dependent. Closest evidence that compression savings can be negated (benignly).
does_not_prove: No adversary; the longer-output effect is not induced deliberately. Does measure serving resource/latency effects. No multi-tenant adversarial setting.
bearing: resource: compression savings negated in serving

title: Rethinking Latency Denial-of-Service: Attacking the LLM Serving Framework, Not the Model
quote: Fill first exhausts the global KV cache to induce Head-of-Line blocking
proves: Adversarial prompts fill KV cache memory and trigger repeated preemption in the scheduler, a serving-level DoS (Fill and Squeeze), using latency probing to estimate free cache.
does_not_prove: Adversary and resource impact both present, and it is a shared serving setting, but it does not involve KV compression or eviction policies at all; does not show forcing dense retention under a compressor.
bearing: adjacent: KV occupancy DoS (no compression); Closest prior art for KV-occupancy exhaustion. Any new KV-exhaustion idea must beat or differ from F&S (e.g., prefix-cache or compression-aware variants, or fair/quota schedulers). Small-model Metal reproduction plausible.

title: Can Transformer Memory Be Corrupted? Investigating Cache-Side Vulnerabilities in Large Language Models
quote: systematically perturbs cached key vectors at selected layers and timesteps
proves: Treats the KV cache as an attack surface: perturbing cached keys propagates silently to outputs.
does_not_prove: Threat model assumes direct write access to cache, not input-only adversary manipulating compression. Output corruption, not memory/resource. No multi-tenant compression path.
bearing: adjacent: KV integrity attacks

title: LLM Jailbreaks Exploit Attention Sinks
quote: We find that tokens in adversarial suffixes are prone to inducing attention sinks
proves: Adversarial suffixes create attention sinks; amplifying them raises jailbreak success. Shows adversarial text can control where attention mass goes, the signal eviction policies score on.
does_not_prove: Adversary present but goal is jailbreak, not eviction or memory; no compression evaluated. No resource or multi-tenant aspect.
bearing: attention-sink manipulation

title: Interpreting the Repeated Token Phenomenon in Large Language Models
quote: the initial token receives disproportionately high attention scores
proves: Links repeated-token divergence to attention-sink mechanics; inputs can perturb sink behavior that StreamingLLM-style compressors rely on.
does_not_prove: Does not evaluate KV compression or eviction; no memory measurement; no serving. Search snippets mention a "cluster attack" but the abstract I saw did not, so not claimed.
bearing: attention-sink manipulation

title: Robust KV Cache Management for LLM Serving under Output Token Length Uncertainty
quote: We present a robust KV cache management framework for LLM serving
proves: Distributionally robust (Wasserstein DRO) KV memory management under output-length uncertainty and workload shift in serving.
does_not_prove: Statistical robustness, no malicious users. Measures memory/serving outcomes. Multi-request serving but not adversarial multi-tenant; not about compression.
bearing: hardening: DRO KV memory under shift

title: A Probabilistic Interpretation of KV Cache Eviction
quote: correcting for evicted entries during decoding---a previously ignored problem---becomes feasible
proves: Recasts eviction probabilistically so the effect of evicted entries can be corrected at decode time; claims more robust than top-k heuristics.
does_not_prove: No adversary; benign tasks. Accuracy, not memory under attack. No multi-tenant.
bearing: hardening: principled eviction correction

title: VeriCache: Turning Lossy KV Cache into Lossless LLM Inference
quote: almost all of these methods are inherently lossy
proves: Proposes making lossy KV compression lossless (verification-style), giving an output guarantee regardless of input. Strongest "guarantee" direction found.
does_not_prove: No adversary studied; an adversary could still raise verification failure rate and cost (not measured). Resource cost of fallback under adversarial input unmeasured. No multi-tenant.
bearing: hardening: lossless guarantee

title: H2O: Heavy-Hitter Oracle for Efficient Generative Inference of Large Language Models
quote: a small portion of tokens contributes most of the value when computing attention scores
proves: Canonical accumulated-attention token eviction (heavy hitters).
does_not_prove: No adversary; benign benchmarks. Memory savings shown, but assumes sparse attention that an input could defeat. No multi-tenant.
bearing: family: token eviction

title: Efficient Streaming Language Models with Attention Sinks (StreamingLLM)
quote: the emergence of attention sink is due to the strong attention scores towards initial tokens
proves: Keep initial sink tokens plus a recent window for bounded-memory streaming.
does_not_prove: No adversary; memory bounded by design (fixed window), so it cannot be forced to max occupancy but can be forced to drop content. No multi-tenant.
bearing: family: token eviction / sinks

title: SnapKV: LLM Knows What You are Looking for Before Generation
quote: this robust pattern can be obtained from an 'observation' window located at the end of the prompts
proves: Prompt-end observation window selects which prefill KV to keep. Relies on query at prompt end, which a user controls.
does_not_prove: No adversary; "robust" means across benign data. Memory/speed measured benignly. No multi-tenant.
bearing: family: token eviction (prefill)

title: PyramidKV: Dynamic KV Cache Compression based on Pyramidal Information Funneling
quote: allocating more cache in lower layers and less in higher ones
proves: Layer-wise budget allocation based on attention funneling.
does_not_prove: No adversary; benign. Fixed budgets, accuracy-focused. No multi-tenant.
bearing: family: layer budgets

title: Ada-KV: Optimizing KV Cache Eviction by Adaptive Budget Allocation for Efficient LLM Inference
quote: Base on this, we propose Ada-KV, the first head-wise adaptive budget allocation strategy.
proves: Head-wise adaptive budget allocation for eviction.
does_not_prove: No adversary. Total budget fixed, so adversary cannot inflate memory but can steer allocation (untested). No multi-tenant.
bearing: family: dynamic budgets

title: Transformers are Multi-State RNNs (TOVA)
quote: We introduce a novel, training-free compression policy
proves: TOVA: evict token with lowest current attention, a fixed-size multi-state view.
does_not_prove: No adversary; benign. No resource-attack measurement. No multi-tenant.
bearing: family: token eviction

title: Scissorhands: Exploiting the Persistence of Importance Hypothesis for LLM KV Cache Compression at Test Time
quote: only pivotal tokens, which had a substantial influence at one step
proves: Persistence-of-importance hypothesis justifying eviction; the assumption DefensiveKV (B5) calls fragile.
does_not_prove: No adversary; hypothesis tested on benign data. No multi-tenant.
bearing: family: token eviction

title: KIVI: A Tuning-Free Asymmetric 2bit Quantization for KV Cache
quote: the key cache should be quantized per-channel
proves: 2-bit asymmetric KV quantization (per-channel keys, per-token values).
does_not_prove: No adversary; outlier-channel assumptions could be attacked by crafted activations (untested). Memory saving fixed ratio, cannot be defeated by input. No multi-tenant.
bearing: family: quantization

title: KVQuant: Towards 10 Million Context Length LLM Inference with KV Cache Quantization
quote: Our method enables serving LLaMA-7B with a context length of up to 1 million on a single A100-80GB GPU
proves: Low-bit KV quantization with outlier handling enabling very long contexts.
does_not_prove: No adversary; dense-and-sparse outlier storage could grow with adversarial outliers (untested). No multi-tenant.
bearing: family: quantization

title: Palu: Compressing KV-Cache with Low-Rank Projection
quote: a KV-Cache compression framework that utilizes low-rank projection to reduce inference-time LLM memory usage.
proves: Low-rank projection compression of KV.
does_not_prove: No adversary; OOD inputs off the calibration subspace untested. No multi-tenant.
bearing: family: low-rank

title: Inference-Time Hyper-Scaling with KV Cache Compression (DMS)
quote: DMS delays token eviction, implicitly merging representations and preserving critical information.
proves: Learned eviction (Dynamic Memory Sparsification) trading cache memory for more reasoning tokens.
does_not_prove: No adversary; learned policy's OOD behavior untested. Memory measured benignly. No multi-tenant.
bearing: family: learned budgets

title: KVzip: Query-Agnostic KV Cache Compression with Context Reconstruction
quote: a query-agnostic KV cache eviction method enabling effective reuse of compressed KV caches
proves: Query-agnostic compression whose compressed cache is reused across queries, i.e. compression baked into a shared/reused prefix.
does_not_prove: No adversary. Reuse of a compressed context across queries (and possibly users) creates a place where one input's compression decisions affect others; not studied. No multi-tenant security analysis.
bearing: family: query-agnostic; reuse

title: NVIDIA kvpress (GitHub repo)
quote: LLM KV cache compression made easy.
proves: NVIDIA library of KV compression presses for Hugging Face transformers pipelines; de facto benchmarking harness.
does_not_prove: No security/adversarial content; README integrates with HF transformers, not vLLM or a production engine. No multi-tenant.
bearing: production: compression library

title: Expected Attention: KV Cache Compression by Estimating Attention from Future Queries Distribution
quote: a comprehensive library to enable researchers to implement and benchmark KV cache compression methods
proves: Closed-form expected-attention scoring from activation statistics; releases KVPress. Scoring assumes a distribution of future queries.
does_not_prove: No adversary; distributional assumption on queries is exactly what OOD/adversarial queries violate (untested). No multi-tenant.
bearing: family: query-agnostic / production library

title: KVzap: Fast, Adaptive, and Faithful KV Cache Pruning
quote: they have not yet been adopted in major inference engines due to speed--accuracy trade-offs
proves: Fast adaptive pruning aimed at engine adoption; states pruning methods are not yet adopted in major inference engines.
does_not_prove: No adversary. Adaptive (input-dependent) pruning ratio means input could choose low compression (untested). No multi-tenant.
bearing: production: engine adoption status

title: SCBench: A KV Cache-Centric Analysis of Long-Context Methods
quote: existing benchmarks often evaluate in single-request, neglecting the full lifecycle of the KV cache in real-world use
proves: Benchmark of compression/sparse methods under shared-context, multi-turn KV reuse.
does_not_prove: Benign benchmarks only, no adversary; accuracy focus; multi-request reuse but not multi-tenant isolation.
bearing: benchmark: KV lifecycle / reuse

title: KV Cache Compression, But What Must We Give in Return? A Comprehensive Benchmark of Long Context Capable Approaches
quote: no existing work has comprehensively benchmarked these methods in a reasonably aligned environment
proves: Aligned benchmark of compression families (quantization, eviction, etc.) on long-context tasks.
does_not_prove: Benign only; no adversary; no memory-attack; no multi-tenant.
bearing: benchmark

title: KVCache-Factory (GitHub repo)
quote: Unified KV Cache Compression Methods for Auto-Regressive Models
proves: Unified implementations (StreamingLLM, H2O, SnapKV, PyramidKV, AdaKV, HeadKV, KIVI, KVQuant, GEAR, etc.), usable as attack testbed.
does_not_prove: No adversarial or security content; research harness, not a serving engine; no multi-tenant.
bearing: benchmark harness

title: RULER: What's the Real Context Size of Your Long-Context Language Models?
quote: almost all models exhibit large performance drops as the context length increases
proves: Synthetic long-context benchmark widely used to score compression (e.g. KVzap on RULER).
does_not_prove: Not about compression itself; benign; no adversary, memory, or multi-tenant.
bearing: benchmark

title: Preserving Admission Responsibility in Multi-Tenant Large Language Model Prefix Caches
quote: A group that materializes new Key-Value (KV) blocks can force another to lose reusable state.
proves: Cross-tenant prefix-cache pollution is a recognized threat: adversary is a legitimate client controlling its own token sequences and timing; one-touch, low-and-slow rotation, and replay pollution patterns; PrefixShield implemented in vLLM 0.10.2 APC on L4/A100 restores victim hit ratio (abstract: 4.92% to 84.87% at 4096-block scale).
does_not_prove: Targets prefix-cache eviction specifically and measures victim hit ratio, but reports P95 TTFT nearly flat, so victim latency/cost harm is not shown as large; defense paper, not an attack-optimization paper; no compression, no offload tier, no adaptive attacker against PrefixShield.
bearing: Most direct overlap with the advisor's 'prefix-cache attack tied to eviction' interest. Gap left: adaptive attacker vs PrefixShield, measured TTFT/cost harm, multi-tier (CPU/LMCache) pollution, and SGLang radix-tree eviction.

title: An Engorgio Prompt Makes Large Language Model Babble on
quote: a malicious user crafts Engorgio prompts to intentionally increase the computation cost and latency of the inference process
proves: White-box optimized prompts suppress EOS so outputs approach max length on many open models; a real-world experiment shows threat to a resource-limited LLM service.
does_not_prove: Output-length/compute inflation only; does not target prefix cache, eviction, or compression explicitly; abstract does not measure effect on other tenants.
bearing: Baseline 'long output' attacker; KV growth is a side effect. F&S reports such model-level attacks are largely isolated by batching.

title: OverThink: Slowdown Attacks on Reasoning LLMs
quote: An adversary conducts the attack by injecting decoy reasoning problems into available content
proves: Indirect injection of decoy problems inflates hidden reasoning tokens (reported up to tens of x) while answers stay correct; common defenses largely ineffective.
does_not_prove: Reasoning-token/compute inflation only; no KV cache, prefix cache, eviction, or compression targeting; no measurement of other tenants in a shared server.
bearing: Shows reasoning models give cheap length amplification that a KV-exhaustion attacker could use as a primitive.

title: Sponge Examples: Energy-Latency Attacks on Neural Networks
quote: increasing energy consumption by a factor of 10 to 200
proves: Founding work: crafted inputs drive models toward worst-case energy and latency, language models especially vulnerable; portable across CPUs, GPUs, ASIC sim.
does_not_prove: Pre-LLM-serving; no KV cache, paging, prefix cache, or batching; no multi-tenant measurement.
bearing: Origin citation for availability attacks; outside 2023-2026 window but defines the class.

title: Fairness in Serving Large Language Models
venue: arXiv (cs.AI, cs.LG, cs.PF); venue not shown on page
quote: We prove a 2x tight upper bound on the service difference between two backlogged clients.
proves: VTC: token-level fair scheduler over continuous batching with a per-client counter; bounds service difference between backlogged clients.
does_not_prove: Fairness of compute/token service, not of KV memory or prefix-cache occupancy; abstract does not consider adversarial clients; no eviction or compression.
bearing: The fairness baseline. Open question: does VTC bound harm when the attacker consumes KV memory or evicts cached prefixes rather than tokens of service?

title: Adversarial Prompts for Acceptance Collapse in Speculative Decoding
quote: On the GSM8K dataset, our attack increases the mean sample time by 62.3% while preserving the task quality.
proves: ADSD adversarial suffixes collapse draft-target acceptance in speculative decoding, wasting compute while output quality holds.
does_not_prove: Targets speculative decoding acceptance, not KV cache, prefix cache, eviction, or compression; per search summary the threat model excludes KV-cache and scheduler manipulation; no other-tenant measurement.
bearing: Adjacent availability vector; shows optimizations with data-dependent speedups can be inverted. Same logic applies to KV compression ratios.

title: Mistletoe: Stealthy Acceleration-Collapse Attacks on Speculative Decoding
quote: a stealthy acceleration-collapse attack against speculative decoding
proves: Jointly optimizes lower drafter-target agreement and semantic preservation; reduces accepted length, collapses speedup and throughput, preserves quality.
does_not_prove: Speculative decoding only; no KV cache, prefix cache, eviction, or compression; no multi-tenant effect measured.
bearing: Second independent 2026 paper; spec-decoding acceptance attacks are covered, not a gap.

title: RepetitionCurse: Measuring and Understanding Router Imbalance in Mixture-of-Experts LLMs under DoS Stress
quote: out-of-distribution prompts can manipulate the routing strategy
proves: OOD repetitive prompts concentrate MoE expert routing, causing device imbalance, TTFT SLA violations, 3.063x end-to-end latency on Mixtral-8x7B.
does_not_prove: MoE expert routing, not KV cache, prefix cache, eviction, or compression; not request-level load balancers; other-tenant effect implied via SLA, not per-tenant measured in abstract.
bearing: Template for 'efficiency optimization becomes DoS vector' framing; analogous framing fits KV compression.

title: ThinkTrap: Denial-of-Service Attacks against Black-box LLM Services via Infinite Thinking
quote: as low as 1% of its original capacity
proves: Black-box derivative-free prompt optimization induces unbounded reasoning; at about 10 RPM the attack degrades service throughput to as low as 1% and sometimes causes complete failure.
does_not_prove: Output/reasoning length attack; does not target KV cache structure, prefix cache, eviction, or compression explicitly; service-wide throughput loss implies other users harmed but no per-tenant KV analysis.
bearing: Shows rate limits in requests do not stop length attacks; motivates token- or KV-based admission.

title: Denial-of-Service Poisoning Attacks against Large Language Models
quote: injecting a single poisoned sample designed for DoS purposes can break the output length limit
proves: Fine-tuning-time poisoning (P-DoS) makes models emit repeated output up to max inference length, including via a commercial fine-tuning API.
does_not_prove: Output length only, via training-data poisoning; no KV cache, prefix cache, eviction, or compression; no multi-tenant measurement.
bearing: Background for length-inflation class; not a serving-system attack.

title: ReasoningBomb: A Stealthy Denial-of-Service Attack by Inducing Pathologically Long Reasoning in Large Reasoning Models
quote: ReasoningBomb induces 18,759 completion tokens on average and 19,263 reasoning tokens on average across reasoning models.
proves: Short prompts induce very long reasoning with large input-to-output amplification, beating prior baselines.
does_not_prove: Token/compute inflation only; no KV cache, prefix, eviction, or compression targeting; abstract reports no effect on other users or throughput.
bearing: Crowded area: reasoning-length DoS has several 2025-2026 papers (OverThink, ThinkTrap, ReasoningBomb).

title: The Multi-Tenant LLM Problem: Noisy Neighbors, Isolation, and Fairness at Scale
quote: One tenant's expensive session evicts another tenant's KV cache, forcing recomputation.
proves: Practitioner acknowledgement that cross-tenant KV eviction raises victim TTFT; argues for token-based rate limiting.
does_not_prove: Opinion piece with no measurement of cross-tenant eviction harm; benign noisy neighbor, not adversarial; no compression.
bearing: Evidence the problem is felt in practice but unmeasured; supports a measurement contribution.

title: CVE-2026-10813: LMCache 16-bit Multimodal Hash Collision Vulnerability
quote: A flaw has been identified in LMCache versions up to 0.4.6.
proves: LMCache KV handler uses a weak 16-bit hash (hex_hash_to_int16) that allows cache poisoning of KV data in the offload tier.
does_not_prove: Integrity (collision/poisoning) of the LMCache tier, not exhaustion or eviction; local, high complexity; no other-tenant availability measurement; aggregator page, NVD not opened.
bearing: Only offload-tier security item found; offload-tier availability (thrashing CPU/disk tiers) appears unstudied.

title: Locality-aware Fair Scheduling in LLM Serving
quote: fail to take prefix locality into consideration
proves: DLPM/D2LPM scheduling keeps prefix locality while giving a fairness guarantee; up to 2.87x throughput over VTC.
does_not_prove: Benign fairness vs locality tradeoff; no adversarial tenant gaming locality or polluting the prefix cache; fairness is over service, not cache occupancy.
bearing: Open question: can an adversary exploit locality-aware schedulers (prefix matching priority) to gain share or evict others.

title: vLLM through 0.29.0 Resource Exhaustion via Ownerless Mooncake Transfer Placeholders (CVE-2026-94625)
quote: causing valid requests to be delayed by up to 480 seconds
proves: Disaggregated prefill/decode KV transfer path in vLLM has a remotely triggerable resource leak that delays other users' valid requests while health checks pass.
does_not_prove: Implementation bug in KV transfer bookkeeping (Mooncake), not KV cache occupancy, prefix cache, eviction, or compression policy; does affect other users.
bearing: Shows KV transfer/offload layers are a live 2026 DoS surface in vLLM; disclosure precedent.

title: Efficient Memory Management for Large Language Model Serving with PagedAttention
quote: this memory can be significantly wasted by fragmentation and redundant duplication
proves: Defines paged KV memory, sharing, and preemption (swap/recompute) mechanisms that later DoS attacks exploit.
does_not_prove: Not a security paper; no adversary, no tenant isolation.
bearing: System background for preemption and block-level sharing.

title: Optimization and Tuning (vLLM v0.19.0 docs, Preemption section)
quote: In such cases, vLLM can preempt requests to free up KV cache space for other requests.
proves: vLLM V1 preempts with RECOMPUTE by default when KV space is insufficient; operator levers are global (gpu_memory_utilization, max_num_seqs, TP).
does_not_prove: Docs only; section mentions no per-tenant KV quota, isolation, or fairness; no adversary.
bearing: Confirms stock vLLM has no per-tenant KV quota, the condition F&S exploits.

title: KVCache Cache in the Wild: Characterizing and Optimizing KVCache Cache at a Large Cloud Provider
quote: KV$ reuses are skewed across requests
proves: Production trace characterization of KV-cache reuse and a workload-aware eviction policy; cited by PrefixShield as source of one-touch pollution pattern.
does_not_prove: Benign workloads only; no tenants, interference, or adversarial pollution per the abstract page.
bearing: Provides realistic traces/baselines for a pollution study; eviction policy itself could be attacked.

title: Rerouting LLM Routers
quote: query-independent token sequences we call ``confounder gadgets''
proves: Gadget strings force model-selection routers to send queries to the expensive model, white-box and black-box.
does_not_prove: Model-selection (cost) routers, not prefix-aware or KV-cache-aware load balancers; no KV, eviction, or compression; no other-tenant load measurement.
bearing: Attacks on prefix-aware/cache-affinity request routers (vLLM production-stack, llm-d) appear unstudied in this search.

title: Cache Me, Catch You: Cache Related Security Threats in LLM Serving Frameworks
quote: manipulate cache entries to deliver malicious content to users via prefix cache collisions
proves: Prefix-cache collision and poisoning vectors exist in vLLM, SGLang, and other frameworks; disclosed and partly fixed.
does_not_prove: Integrity attacks on prefix cache; page excerpt mentions no availability, DoS, or eviction.
bearing: Neighbor class (integrity); combine with pollution for availability is unclaimed.

title: Equinox: Holistic Fair Scheduling in Serving Large Language Models
quote: We address the limitations of current LLM serving with a dual-counter framework separating user and operator perspectives.
proves: Fair scheduling with user and operator counters using predicted tokens and latency.
does_not_prove: No adversarial users mentioned; fairness of service, not KV memory or prefix cache.
bearing: Fairness line keeps growing without an adversarial KV-occupancy model.

title: Ensuring Fair LLM Serving Amid Diverse Applications
quote: some users may submit an excessive number of requests
proves: FairServe uses application-aware throttling and weighted service counters to curb abusive usage on a production multi-tenant platform (MS CoPilot traces).
does_not_prove: Abuse modeled as request volume/tokens, not KV occupancy, prefix eviction, or compression manipulation.
bearing: Closest fairness work that names abusive users; still not memory-aware.

title: LoopLLM: Transferable Energy-Latency Attacks in LLMs via Repetitive Generation
quote: achieving over 90% of the maximum output length, compared to 20% for baselines
proves: Repetition-inducing prompts reach near max output length and transfer to commercial models.
does_not_prove: Output length only; no KV cache, prefix, eviction, or compression; no multi-tenant measurement (F&S uses it as a baseline and finds small TTFT impact).
bearing: Model-level length attacks are mature.

title: CVE-2026-94624: vLLM P2P KV Offloading DoS Vulnerability
quote: The resulting uncaught ZMQError crashes EngineCore and halts all inference on the affected instance.
proves: vLLM P2P KV offloading path through 0.29.0 can be crashed remotely via crafted kv_transfer_params, halting all tenants on the instance.
does_not_prove: Input-validation bug in the offload connector, not a cache-policy or eviction attack; no compression; aggregator page, NVD not opened.
bearing: KV offload/transfer connectors are a fresh bug surface; fuzzing them is engineering, not research novelty.

title: CVE-2026-94627: vLLM Mooncake Connector DOS Vulnerability
quote: Blocks belonging to sibling requests become orphaned and remain resident in GPU memory.
proves: KV block ownership bug in disaggregated serving leaks GPU KV blocks until restart, eventually blocking legitimate requests.
does_not_prove: Leak bug in KV bookkeeping, not policy-level eviction or compression; aggregator page.
bearing: Another KV-memory availability bug; shows KV accounting correctness under adversarial request shapes is weak.

title: Automatic Prefix Caching (design doc)
quote: the freed blocks are added to the tail of the free queue in the reverse order
proves: vLLM evicts prefix-cached blocks from one LRU free queue; sha256 is default block hash since v0.11; per-request salt is offered to block timing attacks on content.
does_not_prove: Salt only partitions hash namespace; the free queue and eviction order are global, so a tenant's allocations still evict another tenant's cached blocks (eviction-contention channel untouched).
bearing: High: core mechanism for eviction-based prefix-cache attacks; single shared LRU is the attack surface the advisor named.

title: Security (Prefix Cache Timing Side-Channel Mitigation; multi-tenant isolation)
quote: Options such as `cache_salt` reduce specific cross-tenant risks, but they are not an isolation boundary.
proves: vLLM officially states it gives no tenant isolation inside one process; cache_salt is opt-in, secret, and only mixed into the first block hash; recommends a dedicated instance per tenant.
does_not_prove: Doc does not quantify residual channels (eviction, preemption, memory pressure, batch interference) and offers no shared-pool partitioning.
bearing: High: maintainers concede the gap; a measured residual channel under salting would be directly relevant upstream.

title: [RFC]: Cache Salting for Secure and Flexible Prefix Caching in vLLM (#16016)
quote: We propose to salt block hashes by introducing an optional top-level field in the request schema
proves: Origin RFC for cache_salt, motivated by Leaking Secrets from Prefix Caches; considered single-barrier and multi-barrier (per-message) designs.
does_not_prove: Threat model is content inference via hit/miss timing only; eviction and capacity contention are out of scope.
bearing: High: defines the threat model upstream accepted, so anything outside it is a candidate gap.

title: [Core] Prevent side-channel attacks via cache salting (#17045)
quote: When present, the salt is injected into the hash of the first block, ensuring that only requests with the same salt can share cached blocks.
proves: Merged 2025-04-30; implements single-barrier salt in the first block hash.
does_not_prove: Does not change allocator, free queue, or eviction; salted and unsalted blocks still compete for the same pool.
bearing: High: baseline defense any eviction-channel attack must defeat.

title: GHSA-rm76-4mrf-v9r8 / CVE-2025-25183: built-in hash() predictable collisions in prefix cache
quote: Maliciously constructed prompts can lead to hash collisions, resulting in prefix cache reuse, which can interfere with subsequent responses
proves: Shows a real cache-poisoning class: predictable block hashes let an attacker pre-populate KV that another prompt reuses; fixed by random seeding, later sha256 default.
does_not_prove: Does not show a practical collision attack was demonstrated in the wild; with sha256 the collision route is closed.
bearing: Medium: closed integrity path; useful as history and to frame poisoning via other key-construction bugs.

title: GHSA-4qjh-9fv9-r85r / CVE-2025-46570: Potential Timing Side-Channel Vulnerability in vLLM's Chunk-Based Prefix Caching
quote: By measuring the TTFT based on prefix matches, the attacker could verify if their guess is correct
proves: vLLM accepted TTFT prefix-hit timing as a CVE; cache_salt (PR 17045) is the documented fix.
does_not_prove: Covers hit/miss membership only; nothing on eviction-induced or memory-pressure signals.
bearing: High: the canonical CVE; eviction-based variants under salting would be a distinct follow-on.

title: GHSA-935w-9g4m-p28p / CVE-2026-105752: Harmony tool continuations drop cache_salt, restoring a cross-tenant prefix-cache membership oracle
quote: The continuation prefix is therefore cached in the global *unsalted* namespace even though the caller opted into salting.
proves: Salt propagation is fragile; a dropped salt on one path re-opens the membership oracle, read via exact cached-token counts in usage (not timing).
does_not_prove: A propagation bug, not a flaw in salting itself; does not touch eviction.
bearing: Medium: shows usage fields (cached_tokens) are a noiseless oracle channel; useful for measurement design.

title: GHSA-rh6f-3x46-j33q: caller-controllable values collide with shared cache keys (multimodal EXIF hash and prefix-cache extra keys)
quote: a request under static LoRA `foo` and a base-model request with `cache_salt="foo"` both yield first-block `extra_keys = ("foo",)` and the identical `BlockHash`
proves: Cross-domain key aliasing let a chosen salt reuse KV produced under a LoRA adapter: cache poisoning/aliasing via key construction, not hash weakness.
does_not_prove: Key-construction bug; says nothing about shared-pool contention.
bearing: Medium: integrity side of KV sharing; supports a key-partition invariant checker as a contribution.

title: GHSA-vfp2-c8pq-v6h6: SSRF via X-Request-Id drives P2pNcclConnector, leaking KV-cache tensors
quote: Any API client that can reach a prefill worker running `P2pNcclConnector` can exfiltrate the full KV-cache
proves: Disaggregated KV transfer has had a direct KV exfiltration bug (vLLM 0.9.2 to <0.24.0); connector removed.
does_not_prove: Not a side channel; an input-validation bug in one connector.
bearing: Low-Medium: shows KV transfer plane is an attack surface; outside the eviction focus.

title: [RFC]: A conformance suite for KV-cache key partitioning (#53194)
quote: They are not ten bugs. They are one missing invariant, observed ten times.
proves: At least ten defects where cache_salt, LoRA, or prompt_embeds failed to partition KV keys across tiers (LMCache, HF3FS, Harmony, embeddings); proposes one conformance suite.
does_not_prove: Partition is about key namespace only; the suite would not test eviction, capacity, or timing interference.
bearing: High: upstream is converging on key-partition invariants; resource-partition invariants are the visible missing next step.

title: [Core] Make prefix-cache NONE_HASH deterministic by default (#51875)
quote: `cache_salt` is the supported mechanism for intentional cache isolation.
proves: Merged 2026-08-18: block hashes are now identical across instances by default, so an attacker can compute victim block hashes offline.
does_not_prove: Does not by itself leak data; relevant only when hashes are exposed (KV events, external stores, routers).
bearing: Medium: makes hash precomputation and cross-node prefix probing easier; ties to router/KV-event surfaces.

title: vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py FreeKVCacheBlockQueue
quote: 1. The least recent used block is at the front (LRU).
proves: One doubly linked free-block queue per KV cache manager orders eviction by recency then chain tail; no per-salt or per-tenant structure exists.
does_not_prove: Code read only; did not run an eviction experiment.
bearing: High: concrete code target for a cross-salt eviction (Prime+Probe style) kill-test on the M5 setup.

title: Optimization and Tuning: Preemption
quote: the default preemption mode is `RECOMPUTE` rather than `SWAP`
proves: When KV space runs out, vLLM preempts and recomputes requests; this is a global, cross-tenant reaction to memory pressure.
does_not_prove: Doc frames preemption as performance tuning; no security discussion or tenant fairness.
bearing: High: forced preemption of other tenants via KV-hungry requests is a denial/inference channel salting does not address.

title: [Feature]: Priority scheduling is not reflected in KV/prefix cache retention under cache pressure (#47802)
quote: Under KV cache pressure, high-priority requests are not protected from losing cached prompt tokens compared with low-priority requests.
proves: Measured on vLLM 0.19.0: retention is priority-blind; any request can evict anyone's cached prefix.
does_not_prove: Performance framing, not adversarial; one model and setup.
bearing: High: independent evidence that eviction is a shared, unprotected resource.

title: [Feature]: Per-request prefix-cache miss attribution (prompt divergence vs. eviction) (#60044)
quote: The prefix was cached earlier but got pushed out under memory pressure.
proves: Users want per-request signal of eviction-caused misses; cached_tokens already exposed per request.
does_not_prove: A feature request; not implemented as of fetch.
bearing: Medium: if shipped, it would expose an explicit eviction oracle to clients, a new side channel to flag.

title: [Security] Inject Cache Salt By Header (#57609)
quote: The header takes precedence over `cache_salt` in the body, so a client cannot escape the partition its gateway assigned.
proves: Open PR to let a trusted gateway enforce per-tenant salt via X-Cache-Salt.
does_not_prove: Still namespace-only; no capacity quota per salt.
bearing: Medium: upstream moving toward gateway-enforced tenant salts, which makes salted multi-tenant pools the realistic deployment to attack.

title: GHSA-wpww-v874-ph2p / CVE-2026-100647: unbounded cache_salt length stalls EngineCore scheduler
quote: vLLM DoS via unbounded `cache_salt` length: multi-hundred-MB salt stalls the single EngineCore scheduler thread (CPU exhaustion)
proves: The isolation feature itself became a resource-exhaustion vector (seen as advisory summary via gh api).
does_not_prove: Only the summary was read; body not reviewed. CPU DoS, not KV memory.
bearing: Low-Medium: shows resource-consumption attacks against cache machinery are accepted as CVEs.

title: [RFC]: Sparse KV cache management framework (#12254)
quote: Evicting potentially many low-utilization tokens, especially in long context, is the way to do it.
proves: Proposed pluggable CachePolicy (sliding window, H2O, FastGen) for token eviction; issue is closed.
does_not_prove: No adversarial analysis; closed, so no shipped token-level KV compression policy in vLLM core is shown here.
bearing: Medium: compression-manipulation attacks have no mainline vLLM target; research would need kvpress/HF or a fork.

title: [Feature]: KVPress (#10491)
quote: This repository implements multiple KV cache pruning methods and benchmarks using [🤗 transformers]
proves: Request to integrate NVIDIA kvpress; closed.
does_not_prove: Closed request only; no integration shipped per this issue.
bearing: Medium: confirms kvpress lives outside vLLM; adversarial compression work targets research stacks, not production engines.

title: Possible timing side-channels caused by shared prefix (#1504)
quote: if the `TokenKVPool` has its prefix tokens, the prefill process will be accelerated, which can be reflected in TTFT
proves: Researchers reported token-granularity RadixAttention timing leak to SGLang in 2024 (linked to arXiv 2409.20002).
does_not_prove: Report only; does not show eviction-based leakage or a shipped fix in that thread.
bearing: Medium: token-level radix sharing gives finer probes than block-level vLLM.

title: python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/radix_cache.py (RadixKey cache_salt, eviction strategy)
quote: # Namespaces the tree, storage and KV events.
proves: SGLang now carries cache_salt in RadixKey; one radix tree with a configurable eviction strategy (LRU default when disabled) and priority-aware eviction.
does_not_prove: Salt namespaces tree keys but eviction runs over one evictable_leaves set for the whole tree.
bearing: High: second engine with the same shared-eviction structure; cross-engine generality of an eviction attack.

title: LMCache integration ignores per-request cache_salt: external storage keys are token-only, breaking tenant isolation (#37160)
quote: a second account's identical prefix served from the first account's cache (1198 ms) against a 3430 ms recompute baseline
proves: End-to-end measured cross-tenant hit through the L3 LMCache tier despite salting.
does_not_prove: Propagation bug in one integration; open at fetch time.
bearing: Medium: lower tiers routinely drop isolation; tiered caches widen the attack surface.

title: [Bug] /v1/responses silently drops prompt_cache_key instead of applying it to radix-cache identity (#37263)
quote: so requests from distinct caller cache keys all enter the global radix-cache namespace
proves: OpenAI-compatible prompt_cache_key is being mapped to engine salt; without it all callers share one namespace.
does_not_prove: Bug report; fix planned, not verified.
bearing: Low-Medium: shows engines adopting provider API semantics for isolation.

title: KV Cache System (cache salting, prioritized LRU eviction, host offload)
quote: Only requests with matching cache salt values can share cached KV blocks.
proves: TRT-LLM ships cache_salt plus prioritized LRU (priority 0-100, default 35) and optional host offload.
does_not_prove: Salt partitions reuse, not eviction; caller-set retention priority could let one tenant pin blocks and push others out.
bearing: High: priority-controlled eviction is a new knob an adversary may abuse to force others' evictions.

title: lmcache/v1/distributed/eviction_policy/isolated_lru.py (IsolatedLRU per-cache_salt eviction)
quote: this policy keeps one LRU list per ``cache_salt``
proves: Only shipped per-salt eviction isolation found: LMCache L2 tier keeps one LRU per salt with per-salt quota.
does_not_prove: Applies to LMCache L2 storage, not GPU KV in vLLM/SGLang; D26 shows it breaks on L1.
bearing: High: closest existing defense to eviction isolation; a natural baseline to port to GPU block pools.

title: --eviction-policy IsolatedLRU permanently kills the L1 eviction thread on the first over-watermark cycle (#4817)
quote: selecting it silently disables L1 eviction for the lifetime of the server
proves: IsolatedLRU is not usable on L1; per-salt eviction exists only in a lower tier and is immature.
does_not_prove: Bug report; fix PR #4818 open (rejects IsolatedLRU on L1).
bearing: Medium: confirms per-tenant eviction isolation is not production-ready on hot tiers.

title: llm-d-kv-cache README (KV-Cache Indexer, KVEvents)
quote: It is powered by `KVEvents` streamed from vLLM, which provide structured metadata as KV-blocks are created or evicted
proves: llm-d keeps a fleet-wide index of which pod holds which block hashes, fed by vLLM stored/evicted events, for prefix-aware routing.
does_not_prove: README does not describe tenant isolation of the index or routing decisions.
bearing: High: the router and event stream are a cluster-level shared structure; routing choice itself may leak cache state.

title: Should preciseprefixcache honor cache_salt? (#1389)
quote: Two requests with identical prompts but different `cache_salt` values would produce distinct prefix-cache keys under the approximate prefix-cache but identifical cache keys under the precise prefix cache.
proves: Router-level salt handling lagged engine salting; maintainers agreed precise routing must respect salt.
does_not_prove: Closed; fix (#1445) suggested but not verified here.
bearing: Medium: routers are a separate isolation layer that repeatedly drifts from engine semantics.

title: SGLang cache_salt is not honored by precise prefix-cache routing (#3143)
quote: As a result, requests with different salts can match the same cached prefix
proves: Open as of 2026-10: router indexes SGLang blocks unsalted, so cross-salt routing hits are possible.
does_not_prove: Routing match is not KV reuse inside the engine; leak is via routing/placement, not content.
bearing: Medium: placement-based side channel candidate (routed-to-pod latency) even when engines isolate.

title: Router Design (Dynamo KV router)
quote: The KVIndexer builds and maintains a global view of cached blocks in a prefix tree.
proves: Dynamo routes by prefix overlap using KV stored/removed events from workers.
does_not_prove: Doc has no salt, tenant, or security statement.
bearing: Medium: second cluster router with the same global prefix-tree structure.

title: fix(epp): preserve cache namespace and salt parity (#13426)
quote: Verify request-side selection hashes and worker KV-event hashes are isolated and match
proves: Dynamo is adding salt parity between router and worker events; tenant auth explicitly out of scope.
does_not_prove: Closed issue; does not address shared capacity or routing load signals.
bearing: Medium: convergence on salt as the isolation primitive across the stack.

title: Prompt caching (OpenAI API guide)
quote: Caches are not shared across organizations and cannot be reused across
proves: OpenAI isolates per org, routes by a hash of initial tokens, prompt_cache_key influences routing and helps prevent cache-hit probing across users; overflow above 15 requests per minute.
does_not_prove: Inside one org, users share caches unless keys differ; no statement on eviction contention, machine sharing across orgs, or memory-pressure effects.
bearing: High: provider-level isolation is org namespace plus routing; cross-org eviction on shared machines is not addressed.; beneficiary: cost savings justify caching; within-org sharing is the residual attack surface

title: Prompt caching (Claude API docs)
quote: Caches are isolated between organizations. Different organizations never share caches, even if they use identical prompts.
proves: Anthropic isolates per org and per workspace (Claude API, AWS, Foundry); Bedrock and Google Cloud use org-level isolation; 5-minute default TTL, 1-hour option.
does_not_prove: Statement covers content sharing; silent on whether orgs share hardware, eviction queues, or capacity.
bearing: High: same gap as OpenAI; a cross-org eviction channel would sit outside the stated guarantee.

title: Context caching (Gemini API)
quote: Implicit caching is enabled by default for all Gemini 2.5 and newer models.
proves: Gemini runs implicit prefix caching by default.
does_not_prove: The page has no isolation or sharing statement (checked); Vertex doc fetch did not return body text.
bearing: Medium: isolation scope undocumented for a default-on cache.; beneficiary: default-on caching widens the population exposed to cache timing

title: Context Caching (DeepSeek API guide)
quote: The DeepSeek API Context Caching on Disk Technology is enabled by default for all users
proves: DeepSeek caches prefixes on disk by default; entries cleared within hours to days; matches only full prefix units.
does_not_prove: The page fetched has no isolation statement; disk-tier eviction behaviour not described.
