venue: arXiv 2512.12008; NeurIPS 2025 virtual listing (likely workshop, not confirmed)
quote: eviction strategies at low budgets can produce longer reasoning traces, revealing a tradeoff between cache size and inference costs
proves: For non-reasoning Llama-3.1-8B no single strategy wins and results depend heavily on dataset type; for reasoning models H2O and decode-time SnapKV dominate; low budgets lengthen reasoning traces.
does_not_prove: Accuracy and trace length only; no serving throughput measurement of the length-inflation cost.
bearing: per-task variance; output-length inflation under compression (serving cost)

title: ThinKV: Thought-Adaptive KV Cache Compression for Efficient Reasoning Models
quote: attention sparsity reveals distinct thought types with varying importance within the CoT
proves: Hybrid quantization-eviction keyed to thought type, with a PagedAttention-extending kernel reusing evicted slots; <5% KV with near-lossless accuracy and up to 5.8x throughput over baselines on math and code.
does_not_prove: Thought-type classifier tuned on reasoning traces; behavior on non-reasoning or mixed workloads not shown.
bearing: reasoning-aware compression; serving kernel

title: G-KV: Decoding-Time KV Cache Eviction with Global Attention
quote: existing methods often focus on prompt compression or token eviction with local attention score, overlooking the long-term importance of tokens
proves: Decode-time eviction for reasoning combining local and historical attention; adds RL and distillation to adapt models to compressed caches.
does_not_prove: Abstract gives no numbers; model post-training makes it less of a drop-in serving option.
bearing: decode-time eviction for reasoning

title: LazyEviction: Lagged KV Eviction with Attention Pattern Observation for Efficient Long Reasoning
venue: arXiv 2506.15969 (ACL 2026 long per ACL Anthology preview)
quote: a large proportion of tokens regain high attention after multiple decoding steps
proves: Token Importance Recurrence in reasoning traces breaks greedy eviction; lagged eviction keeps 50-70% reduction with comparable accuracy.
does_not_prove: No serving integration; reasoning workloads only.
bearing: workload-specific attention dynamics (reasoning)

title: Which Heads Matter for Reasoning? RL-Guided KV Cache Compression (RLKV)
quote: head-reallocation methods, designed for retrieval tasks, fail to preserve the heads essential for generative reasoning
proves: Retrieval-head selection (DuoAttention/RazorAttention style) does not transfer to reasoning; RL-found reasoning heads allow 20-60% reduction, up to 2.06x end-to-end speedup.
does_not_prove: Head selection is per model; transfer to other workload types not shown.
bearing: head-budget transfer failure across task types

title: Kitty: Accurate and Efficient 2-bit KV Cache Quantization with Dynamic Channel-wise Precision Boost
quote: While 4-bit KV quantization preserves accuracy, 2-bit often degrades it, especially on long-context reasoning
proves: 2-bit KV quantization degrades most on long-context reasoning (secondary summary: KIVI-K2V2 ~13 pts below FP16 on AIME with 32k generations); mixed-precision paged layout gives up to 8x batch and 2.1-4.1x throughput.
does_not_prove: AIME figure from search summary, not verified in PDF.
bearing: quantization fragility on long decode; serving co-design

title: KVarN: Variance-Normalized KV-Cache Quantization Mitigates Error Accumulation in Reasoning Tasks
quote: current methods are evaluated under prefill-like settings and errors behave differently under autoregressive decoding
proves: KV quantization errors accumulate over decode steps (driven by token-scale errors); prefill-style evaluation hides this. vLLM implementation released.
does_not_prove: Math and HumanEval only; no serving throughput in abstract.
bearing: evaluation-regime shift (prefill vs decode); quantization error accumulation

title: MixKVQ: Query-Aware Mixed-Precision KV Cache Quantization for Long-Context Reasoning
venue: arXiv 2512.19206 (ACL 2026 long per ACL Anthology preview)
quote: existing low-bit quantization methods often exhibit severe performance degradation on complex reasoning tasks
proves: Low-bit KV quantization fails on reasoning due to key outlier channels; query-aware channel precision fixes it.
does_not_prove: No serving evaluation; reasoning datasets only.
bearing: quantization fragility by task type

title: KV-CoRE: Benchmarking Data-Dependent Low-Rank Compressibility of KV-Caches in LLMs
quote: uncovering systematic patterns that link compressibility to model architecture, training data, and language coverage
proves: Only large-scale evidence found on language dependence: KV compressibility measured over 5 English domains and 16 languages; Normalized Effective Rank correlates with degradation under compression.
does_not_prove: Low-rank compressibility only (not eviction or quantization); per-language degradation numbers not in abstract.
bearing: multilingual/domain dependence of compressibility; predictor of degradation

title: The Sparse Frontier: Sparse Attention Trade-offs in Transformer LLMs
venue: arXiv 2504.17768 (ACL 2026 Findings per ACL Anthology preview)
quote: longer sequences tolerate higher sparsity, suggesting that fixed-budget methods in production are suboptimal
proves: Largest training-free sparse attention study (6 methods, 9 tasks, up to 128K): prefill selection choice is task-dependent; fixed budgets are suboptimal across lengths.
does_not_prove: Accuracy/compute analysis; no serving throughput under mixed workloads.
bearing: task dependence; fixed-budget critique

title: Twilight: Adaptive Attention Sparsity with Hierarchical Top-p Pruning
quote: fails to account for the dynamic nature of real-world scenarios, where the optimal balance between accuracy and efficiency can vary greatly
proves: Top-p (mass-based) budget makes any sparse attention adaptive per input; prunes up to 98% tokens, 3.9x per-token latency.
does_not_prove: Adaptive budget means cost becomes input-dependent; abstract does not evaluate worst-case (dense-attention) inputs or batch-level variance.
bearing: adaptive budget; input-dependent cost (resource-variance risk)

title: FlexPrefill: A Context-Aware Sparse Attention Mechanism for Efficient Long-Sequence Inference
quote: dynamically adjusts sparse attention patterns and computational budget in real-time to meet the specific requirements of each input and attention head
proves: Input-adaptive prefill sparsity using JS divergence and cumulative-attention thresholds.
does_not_prove: Prefill compute only; compute becomes input-dependent; no serving or adversarial worst-case analysis.
bearing: adaptive budget; input-dependent cost

title: Adaptive KV-Cache Compression without Manually Setting Budget (GVote)
venue: arXiv 2509.03136 (ICLR 2026 per search summary, not confirmed)
quote: they force diverse workloads into fixed compression ratios, leading to suboptimal resource allocation and inference performance
proves: Sampled future queries set the per-input cache budget; 2x memory reduction on GSM8K, RULER, LongBench.
does_not_prove: Memory per request becomes input-dependent; no serving-level capacity planning or worst-case input study.
bearing: adaptive budget; fixed-ratio critique

title: ReFreeKV: Towards Threshold-Free KV Cache Compression
quote: the dependence of such input-sensitive threshold can be a fundamental limitation that causes large degradation on arbitrary inputs
proves: States that fixed budgets tuned per domain degrade on arbitrary open-domain inputs; proposes adaptive threshold-free budget across 13 datasets.
does_not_prove: Accuracy-centric; memory variance per request in serving not analyzed.
bearing: direct robustness framing: input-sensitive budgets; adaptive budget

title: DynamicKV: Task-Aware Adaptive KV Cache Compression for Long Context LLMs
quote: we observe distinct activation patterns across layers in various tasks
proves: Layer activation patterns differ by task; task-adaptive per-layer budgets; 1.7% KV keeps ~85% LongBench.
does_not_prove: No serving evaluation.
bearing: task-dependent layer budgets

title: LAVa: Layer-wise KV Cache Eviction with Dynamic Budget Allocation
quote: dynamic layer budgets are crucial for generation tasks (e.g., code completion), while dynamic head budgets play a key role in extraction tasks (e.g., extractive QA)
proves: Which budget dimension matters depends on task type (generation vs extraction); other methods' rankings shift across task types.
does_not_prove: No serving evaluation.
bearing: per-task variance of eviction policy rankings

title: CAKE: Cascading and Adaptive KV Cache Eviction with Layer Preferences
quote: CAKE assesses layer-specific preferences by considering attention dynamics in both spatial and temporal dimensions
proves: Input-adaptive layer budgets; 3.2% KV on LongBench/NeedleBench; >10x decode latency speedup at 128K.
does_not_prove: No serving-level batching study.
bearing: adaptive per-layer budgets

title: Not All Heads Matter: A Head-Level KV Cache Compression Method with Integrated Retrieval and Reasoning (HeadKV)
quote: estimating their importance for contextual QA tasks that require both retrieval and reasoning capabilities
proves: Head budgets estimated offline for contextual QA; 1.5% KV gives 97% of full on contextual QA.
does_not_prove: Head importance tuned for QA; RLKV later shows such retrieval-tuned head selection fails on reasoning.
bearing: offline head budgets; task-specific calibration

title: CompilerKV: Risk-Adaptive KV Compression via Offline Experience Compilation
quote: these signals exhibit far higher cross-prompt regularity than within-prompt signal-to-noise
proves: Online per-prompt sensitivity estimates are noisy; offline-compiled tables transfer across disjoint corpora (Spearman 0.90); under 512/32k budget, SnapKV ~38 vs CompilerKV ~73 vs FullKV ~79 on 128k RULER; batch-16 feasible where FullKV OOMs.
does_not_prove: Transfer tested across corpora, not across task types like reasoning or multilingual; no adversarial inputs.
bearing: calibration transfer evidence; budget-pressure amplification

title: KV-COBRA: KV Cache Compression via Co-Optimized Bit-Rank Allocation
quote: each head has a different optimal mix of rank truncation and quantization
proves: Per-head bit/rank allocation; paper (per search snippet) reports calibration on Python vs WikiText-2 moves HumanEval by at most 1.6 points.
does_not_prove: Calibration-transfer claim seen only in search snippet; abstract does not state it.
bearing: calibration robustness (counter-evidence: allocation transfers)

title: CodeComp: Structural KV Cache Compression for Agentic Coding
quote: systematically discarding structurally critical tokens such as call sites, branch conditions, and assignments
proves: Attention-only eviction drops code-structural tokens; program-analysis priors fix it; integrates into SGLang agentic coding pipelines.
does_not_prove: Code-specific; no throughput-under-load data in abstract.
bearing: code workload failure mode; SGLang integration

title: KVDiagnosis: A Diagnostic Benchmark for KV-Cache Compression in Long-Context Language Models
quote: aggregate task scores reveal neither which correct executions fail nor why
proves: Per-instance failure diagnosis: 12,520 full-correct/compressed-wrong rows on Qwen3-8B; diagnostics separate failures (AUROC 0.684-0.871).
does_not_prove: Accuracy diagnostics only; one model.
bearing: per-instance failure prediction (could seed a robustness monitor)

title: SCOPE: Optimizing Key-Value Cache Compression in Long-context Generation
quote: Deviation of heavy hitters occurs in the reasoning tasks with long outputs
proves: Prefill-only compression and fixed heavy hitters break on long-output tasks (LongGenBench); separate prefill/decode policies.
does_not_prove: No serving evaluation.
bearing: long-output workload shift

title: RetroInfer: A Vector Storage Engine for Scalable Long-Context LLM Inference
quote: prior sparse attention approaches struggle to balance accuracy and retrieval cost due to varying sparsity patterns
proves: Varying sparsity patterns across inputs hurt prior sparse attention; accuracy-bounded vector index gives up to 4.4x decode throughput at 120K.
does_not_prove: Long-context single-request focus; no mixed workload serving.
bearing: sparsity varies by input; offload system

title: SGLang: Efficient Execution of Structured Language Model Programs
quote: The runtime accelerates execution with novel optimizations like RadixAttention for KV cache reuse
proves: Defines the radix-tree prefix cache (RadixAttention) with LRU leaf eviction that later SGLang work and many papers use as baseline.
does_not_prove: Abstract shows benign benchmark programs only; no workload-shift, OOD, overload, or multi-tenant interference evaluation.
bearing: Baseline mechanism whose LRU eviction is the thing to stress under mix shift.

title: Marconi: Prefix Caching for the Era of Hybrid LLMs
quote: novel admission and eviction policies that more judiciously assess potential cache entries
proves: Admission plus eviction beyond LRU for hybrid (SSM+attention) models; reports up to 34.4x token hit-rate gain over prior prefix caching.
does_not_prove: Average-case gains on benign traces per abstract; no reported adversarial or shifted-mix test; no tenant interference measurement.
bearing: Shows admission control (not just eviction) matters; hybrid-model state makes one-off long prompts costlier to admit.

title: KVFlow: Efficient Prefix Caching for Accelerating LLM-Based Multi-Agent Workflows
quote: evict KV caches using a Least Recently Used (LRU) policy
proves: Argues LRU fails to anticipate future agent usage; uses workflow step graph to prioritize eviction and prefetch.
does_not_prove: Assumes a known agent workflow graph; no test of mispredicted or shifting workflows; no multi-tenant interference.
bearing: Workflow-aware eviction relies on structure that breaks under OOD agent behavior; a robustness gap.

title: KVCache Cache in the Wild: Characterizing and Optimizing KVCache Cache at a Large Cloud Provider
quote: for a specific request category, the pattern tends to be predictable
proves: Alibaba production traces: ideal hit rates 62% and 54% (Traces A/B); single-turn requests give 97% of Trace B hits; reuse time differs by category; daytime vs 3-4 am distributions differ; workload-aware eviction gives 28.3-41.9% QTTFT reduction.
does_not_prove: Characterizes diurnal and category variation but the policy is tuned on those traces; no adversarial or OOD category-mix test; no per-tenant isolation measurement.
bearing: Strongest production evidence that reuse is category-dependent, so policies keyed on category can be misled by category shift.

title: Mooncake: A KVCache-centric Disaggregated Architecture for LLM Serving
quote: Mooncake faces challenges due to highly overloaded scenarios
proves: Kimi production system with multi-tier KV pool; explicitly targets overload with prediction-based early rejection.
does_not_prove: Overload is handled by rejection; abstract gives no worst-case analysis of the rejection predictor or of hit rate under mix shift; no tenant fairness.
bearing: Production admission-control-under-overload precedent tied to KV capacity.

title: Mooncake FAST'25 Trace Release (README)
quote: Identical hash IDs indicate reusable prefix KV cache blocks.
proves: Public 1-hour conversation (12,031 req, avg input 12,035) and tool/agent (23,608 req, avg input 8,596) traces with 512-token prefix block hashes, enabling hit-rate replay.
does_not_prove: One hour only, so no diurnal or long-term shift; anonymized, no tenant IDs, so no multi-tenant interference study possible.
bearing: Directly replayable on a laptop to measure eviction-policy hit rate under synthetic mix shifts.

title: Cost-Efficient Large Language Model Serving for Multi-turn Conversations with CachedAttention
quote: scheduler-aware fetching and eviction schemes
proves: Hierarchical KV caching across GPU/host/disk with scheduler-hinted eviction and prefetch for multi-turn chat.
does_not_prove: Benign multi-turn workloads; no evaluation of hint quality under shift or of tier thrash under one-off long prompts; no tenant isolation.
bearing: Multi-tier caching depends on scheduler foresight; a lever that degrades when arrivals shift.

title: Preble: Efficient Distributed Prompt Scheduling for LLM Serving
quote: co-optimizes KV state reuse and computation load-balancing
proves: Cache-aware distributed routing that trades prefix locality against load balance.
does_not_prove: Abstract reports benign workloads; no hot-prefix skew shift or adversarial imbalance; no tenant interference.
bearing: Cache-aware routing is a second place where shift (hot prefix moves) can cause imbalance.

title: SkyWalker: A Locality-Aware Cross-Region Load Balancer for LLM Inference
quote: SkyWalker preserves KV-Cache locality and load balancing
proves: Cross-region load balancer with a cache-aware traffic handler and selective pushing.
does_not_prove: Focus is regional diurnal load; abstract gives no prefix-popularity-shift stress test or tenant interference measurement.
bearing: Cross-region diurnal shift as a driver of KV locality loss.

title: LMCache: An Efficient KV Cache Layer for Enterprise-Scale LLM Inference
quote: Large-scale adoption of LMCACHE in enterprise settings provides us valuable insights
proves: Open KV offload/sharing layer for vLLM and SGLang; reports context truncation can roughly halve prefix hit ratio in deployments.
does_not_prove: Deployment insights, not a controlled shift study; no worst-case or tenant-interference evaluation in abstract.
bearing: Evidence that a client-side change (truncation) shifts hit rate sharply: a benign OOD trigger.

title: BurstGPT: A Real-world Workload Dataset to Optimize LLM Serving Systems
quote: burstiness variations of requests in Azure OpenAI GPT services
proves: Azure OpenAI trace showing diverse concurrency/burst patterns and service failures.
does_not_prove: No prefix or KV-block content, so hit-rate shift cannot be measured; no tenant-level interference.
bearing: Source of realistic burst arrival processes for stress tests.

title: ServeGen: Workload Characterization and Generation of Large Language Model Serving in Production
quote: The input and output length distributions shift dynamically and independently over time
proves: Alibaba production study: arrivals bursty with shifting rate and burstiness; length distributions shift over time; a few top clients steer the aggregate workload.
does_not_prove: Explicitly says prefix caching was not characterized because request content was withheld; shift is measured but KV hit rate under shift is not.
bearing: Direct production evidence of length/KV-demand shift and client dominance; leaves hit-rate shift open.

title: Azure LLM inference trace 2024 (AzurePublicDataset)
quote: This is a sample of the traces from multiple LLM inference services in Azure, collected on May 10th-19th 2024.
proves: Week-long code and conversation traces with timestamps, context and generated token counts.
does_not_prove: No prompt content or prefix hashes, so prefix hit rate cannot be derived; no tenant IDs.
bearing: Week-scale diurnal KV-demand (context length x rate) variation input for stress tests.

title: DynamoLLM: Designing LLM Inference Clusters for Performance and Energy Efficiency
quote: fluctuations in inference workloads
proves: Exploits workload fluctuation for energy-efficient reconfiguration; backs the Azure 2024 trace.
does_not_prove: Energy/performance reconfiguration, not KV cache policy; no prefix reuse or tenant interference study.
bearing: Context: production fluctuation is large enough to reconfigure clusters around.

title: Llumnix: Dynamic Scheduling for Large Language Model Serving
quote: live migration mechanism for requests and their in-memory states
proves: Migrates requests and KV state across instances to reduce memory fragmentation and preemption, improve isolation and priority.
does_not_prove: Evaluates load imbalance and priorities, but abstract shows no adversarial or OOD mix; isolation is between priorities, not KV quotas per tenant.
bearing: Migration is a memory-pressure relief valve; its worst case under correlated surges is untested.

title: S3: Increasing GPU Utilization during Generative Inference for Higher Throughput
quote: predicts the output sequence length, schedules generation queries based on the prediction
proves: Output-length prediction to reserve KV memory instead of max length, with misprediction handling.
does_not_prove: No analysis of predictor under distribution shift (e.g., reasoning models with long outputs); no tenant interference.
bearing: KV reservation via prediction is the classic component that fails silently under OOD outputs.

title: Efficient LLM Scheduling by Learning to Rank
quote: it is possible to predict the relative ranks of output lengths in a batch of requests
proves: Rank-based output-length prediction for SJF-like scheduling.
does_not_prove: Benign benchmarks; predictor robustness to shifted prompts not tested in abstract; no tenant isolation.
bearing: Predictor-dependent scheduling; candidate for a shift stress test.

title: InferCept: Efficient Intercept Support for Augmented Large Language Model Inference
quote: unnecessary recomputation of already computed contexts
proves: Chooses among preserve/swap/discard of KV during tool-call interceptions to minimize GPU waste.
does_not_prove: Depends on interception duration estimates; no adversarial or shifted tool-latency analysis; no multi-tenant fairness.
bearing: Recompute-vs-swap decision under pauses; agent loops are a key shift case.

title: Fast Distributed Inference Serving for Large Language Models
quote: enable preemption at the granularity of each output token
proves: Token-level preemption with proactive offload/upload of intermediate state to host memory.
does_not_prove: No worst-case analysis of offload thrash under memory pressure; no tenant isolation.
bearing: Preemption + swap baseline for memory-pressure handling.

title: Online Scheduling for LLM Inference with KV Cache Constraints
quote: no deterministic online algorithm can achieve a constant competitive ratio
proves: Formal KV-constrained batching model with hindsight-optimal IP benchmark and lower bound for arbitrary arrivals.
does_not_prove: Theoretical worst case for scheduling, not prefix-cache hit rate; single tenant.
bearing: Worst-case theory exists for KV-constrained scheduling; connects robustness claims to competitive analysis.

title: Optimizing LLM Inference: Fluid-Guided Online Scheduling with Memory Constraints
quote: overflow can evict in-progress requests
proves: Fluid-model stability region and threshold admission (WAIT, Nested WAIT with safety buffer) for KV memory; tested near/at overload.
does_not_prove: Overload tested, but output-length distributions assumed stationary; no prefix-cache interaction; single class.
bearing: KV-aware admission control with stability analysis: closest to a robust admission baseline.

title: Competitive Non-Clairvoyant KV-Cache Scheduling for LLM Inference
quote: a scheduler must minimize latency under a hard memory budget, yet the response lengths of requests are inherently unknown
proves: Prediction-free scheduler with competitive ratio at most 61.92 (32 in large-memory regime).
does_not_prove: Worst-case bound on latency, but constant is large and no prefix reuse or multi-tenant model.
bearing: Shows robustness without predictors is provable for KV scheduling; gap is prefix-cache-aware version.

title: Randomization Boosts KV Caching, Learning Balances Query Load: A Joint Perspective
quote: integrate provably competitive randomized KV cache eviction with learning-based methods
proves: Unified model of eviction and routing; competitive randomized eviction plus learned routing.
does_not_prove: Competitive guarantee covers eviction in its model; abstract does not show production mix shift or tenant interference.
bearing: Closest prior for worst-case-guaranteed prefix eviction; any new robust-eviction claim must beat or extend it.

title: PRISM: Fast Online LLM Serving via Scheduling-Memory Co-design
quote: align request admission with exact-prefix KV retention
proves: Co-designs admission scheduling with radix-tree retention; 23.3-37.1% lower P99 TTFT per QPS than strongest baseline.
does_not_prove: Tail latency measured across load, but no stated OOD or shifted-mix test; no tenant isolation.
bearing: Admission-retention coupling is a recent baseline for shift experiments.

title: PEEK: Predictive Queue-Informed KV Cache Management for LLM Serving
quote: a co-designed eviction hook protects blocks ancestral to queued demand
proves: Uses queued requests to protect needed prefix blocks; gains hold as KV pressure scales on SGLang and vLLM.
does_not_prove: Pressure scaled, but workload shift and tenant interference not stated in abstract.
bearing: Queue-informed eviction is a cheap robustness lever when queues reflect the shifted mix.

title: Not All Tokens Are Worth Caching: Learning Semantic-Aware Eviction for LLM Prefix Caches
quote: existing policies such as LRU largely treat cached blocks uniformly
proves: Online-learned eviction by token type with eviction feedback, claimed adaptive to deployment workloads.
does_not_prove: Online learning adapts, but abstract gives no bound on regret under abrupt shift or under poisoned feedback; no tenant study.
bearing: Learned eviction is exactly where shift robustness (cf. learning-augmented caching) is untested.

title: A Year in LLM Serving: Workload Evolution, Caching and Load-Balancing
quote: they do not fully capture how LLM serving workloads evolve over time
proves: Year-long trace: output lengths trend down, per-user inter-arrival shrinks (agents), reuse bimodal, LRU/FIFO often match complex policies, ARC underperforms at mid sizes, cache-blind routing replicates prefixes.
does_not_prove: Cached-token logging only for final two months, so year-long hit-rate trend is absent; no adversarial test; per-user not per-tenant isolation.
bearing: Best evidence on long-term drift; says simple policies are competitive, raising the bar for any new eviction policy.

title: Continuum: Efficient and Robust Multi-Turn LLM Agent Scheduling with KV Cache Time-to-Live
quote: the method needs to remain robust under limited predictability of tool call durations
proves: Pins agent KV across tool calls with a TTL; evaluated on SWE-Bench and BFCL.
does_not_prove: Robustness is to tool-duration noise, not to mixed agent/non-agent tenants competing for KV; no worst-case bound.
bearing: TTL pinning can starve other classes under shift; interference is open.

title: Token Latency Fairness: Performance Isolation for Multi-Tenant LLM Serving
quote: high-demand workloads from one client can cause latency SLO violations for others
proves: FairInference gives latency isolation accounting for delays from the shared KV cache in GPU memory.
does_not_prove: Directly measures multi-tenant interference; abstract does not state shift/OOD scenarios beyond high-demand clients.
bearing: Closest prior on KV-aware tenant isolation; must be cited and differentiated.

title: KVShare: An LLM Service System with Efficient and Effective Multi-Tenant KV Cache Reuse
quote: a cache-aware scheduler that prioritizes requests based on their KV cache hit rates
proves: Cross-tenant KV sharing with hit-rate-priority scheduling.
does_not_prove: Hit-rate-priority can starve low-hit tenants; no fairness or shift evaluation stated.
bearing: Example of a policy whose average gain may create interference under shift.

title: KV-Cache Wins You Can See: From Prefix Caching in vLLM to Distributed Scheduling with llm-d
quote: Cache-blind schedulers constantly duplicate and evict the same prefixes across different pods.
proves: 150 prefix groups at 73% of cluster KV capacity: precise routing P90 TTFT 0.542 s vs 31.1 s approximate, 92.6 s random.
does_not_prove: Single synthetic benign workload; no shift in prefix popularity, no tenant interference.
bearing: Shows how steep the TTFT cliff is when cache-aware routing loses state: a degradation magnitude to reuse.

title: [RFC] Tail-Optimized LRU (T-LRU): Reducing Tail Latency via Conversation-Aware KV Cache Eviction (vllm#37823)
quote: LRU maximizes cache-hit rate but is **conversation-length blind**
proves: Proposes TTFT-budget-aware eviction for vLLM; claims up to 27.4% lower P95 TTFT on real conversations. Issue state CLOSED.
does_not_prove: Conversation workloads only; no shift or tenant interference.
bearing: Shows upstream interest and that hit-rate-optimal is not tail-optimal.

title: Tail-Optimized Caching for LLM Inference
quote: a metric of central importance to practitioners
proves: T-LRU proven optimal under a stochastic conversation model; lowers P90/P95 TTFT on WildChat vs LRU.
does_not_prove: Optimality is under a stochastic model, not adversarial or shifted; no multi-tenant.
bearing: Tail-latency objective for eviction; extending to shift is open.

title: [Feature] Per-request opt-out from prefix cache insertion (skip_cache_insert) (sglang#38069)
quote: displacing opt-in tenants' real prefixes and lowering their hit rate
proves: Production report that never-hittable inserts occupy radix-tree memory until LRU reaches them, hurting other tenants' hit rate; asks for admission opt-out.
does_not_prove: Qualitative; no measurement of the hit-rate loss.
bearing: Direct evidence that missing admission control causes cross-tenant KV interference in SGLang.

title: [RFC] Per-Token-Range KV-Cache Retention Priority (sglang#36208)
quote: Nothing stops the engine from evicting Session A's important prefix to make room for Session B's less-important request
proves: Proposes per-token-range retention priority modeled on TensorRT-LLM KvCacheRetentionConfig.
does_not_prove: Design proposal only; no shift or interference measurement.
bearing: Shows engines lack retention isolation primitives; priority is soft, not a quota.

title: L1 eviction races async L2 store: chunks discarded before offload are never stored (LMCache#5350)
quote: ~19% of requests permanently retrieve only the shared prefix
proves: Under L1 memory pressure, eviction races offload so chunks never reach L2, causing persistent re-prefill.
does_not_prove: Single-tenant shared-prefix repro; bug, not policy evaluation.
bearing: Memory pressure creates a persistent degraded state (metastable-like) in multi-tier KV caches.

title: FIFO Queues are All You Need for Cache Eviction
quote: most objects in skewed workloads will only be accessed once in a short window
proves: S3-FIFO: small probationary FIFO filters one-hit wonders; lowest mean miss ratio on 10 of 14 datasets over 6594 traces.
does_not_prove: Web/KV-store traces, not LLM KV blocks with prefix dependence; robustness is across datasets, not adversarial; no tenant isolation.
bearing: One-off long prompts are one-hit wonders; S3-FIFO-style admission is an untested baseline for prefix caches.

title: SIEVE is Simpler than LRU: an Efficient Turn-Key Eviction Algorithm for Web Caches
quote: SIEVE achieves up to 63.2% lower miss ratio than ARC
proves: Simple lazy-promotion eviction beating ARC on 1559 web traces with lock-free hits.
does_not_prove: Web caches; not evaluated on prefix-tree KV with parent-child dependence; no adversarial/tenant study.
bearing: Cheap scan-resistant baseline to port to radix KV caches.

title: ARC: A Self-Tuning, Low Overhead Replacement Cache
quote: allows one-time se-quential requests to pass through without polluting the cache
proves: Scan-resistant, self-tuning balance of recency and frequency.
does_not_prove: Storage traces; the 2026 LLM trace study finds ARC below LRU at mid sizes, so scan resistance does not transfer automatically.
bearing: Classic answer to the one-off-long-prompt burst; transfer to KV is not guaranteed.

title: Learning Relaxed Belady for Content Distribution Network Caching
quote: uses machine learning to approximate the Belady MIN algorithm
proves: Learned CDN eviction deployed-feasible, 5-24% WAN traffic reduction.
does_not_prove: CDN traces; no guarantee under distribution shift; no multi-tenant isolation.
bearing: Template for learned prefix-cache eviction and its shift risk.

title: Competitive caching with machine learned advice
quote: naively following the oracle's recommendations may lead to very poor performance
proves: Learning-augmented caching with O(log k) worst-case cap regardless of predictor quality.
does_not_prove: Uniform-size paging model; no LLM prefix structure or tenants.
bearing: Framework for robust learned KV eviction: consistency with good predictions, bounded loss with bad ones.

title: Metastable Failures in Distributed Systems
quote: a trigger causes the system to enter a bad state that persists even when the trigger is removed
proves: Defines metastable failures; notes the root cause is often features that improve efficiency or reliability.
does_not_prove: General distributed systems; no LLM KV measurements.
bearing: Frame for KV cache collapse: a burst evicts hot prefixes, misses raise prefill load, which keeps the cache cold.

title: Metastable Failures in the Wild
quote: categorizing two types of triggers and two types of amplification mechanisms
proves: Empirical study of metastable incidents and amplification mechanisms.
does_not_prove: No LLM serving cases.
bearing: Gives the taxonomy a KV-cache metastability test would use.

title: KPart: A Hybrid Cache Partitioning-Sharing Technique for Commodity Multicores
quote: UCP often hurts performance even though its only goal is to improve it
proves: Strict way-partitioning (CAT-style) can lose performance; hybrid clustering then partitioning recovers it.
does_not_prove: CPU LLC, not KV; workload assumed profiled.
bearing: Analogue: strict per-tenant KV quotas can waste capacity; hybrid share-partition is the lesson.

title: When Fancy Eviction Fails: Rethinking Cache Replacement For LLM Prefix Reuse
quote: Despite a large gap to Belady, sophisticated policies designed for traditional caches provide little benefit over LRU.
proves: 14 eviction algorithms on production traces from two companies (simulation, HBM-constrained and large pool): classic scan-resistant/frequency policies barely beat LRU; large gap to Belady remains; reuse driven by regular session pacing, heavy-tailed footprints, variable miss cost.
does_not_prove: Abstract does not study bursts, mix shift over time, or persistence of degraded hit rate after a burst; simulation, no queueing feedback between misses and load.
bearing: threatens C3 (eviction-policy angle); bounds C2 (policy choice alone may not matter)

title: CacheRoute: Planned Prefix-Affinity Routing for Large-Scale LLM Serving
quote: Prefix caching avoids prefill only when a repeated request returns to a server that still holds the prefix KV.
proves: Cluster-level prefix-affinity routing with shadow replay before enabling affinity; addresses load skew vs locality.
does_not_prove: Abstract does not model feedback between recompute load and eviction or persistence after bursts.
bearing: adjacent to C2 (cluster scale)

title: PrefixBench-H100: Characterizing Prefix Reuse and Time-to-First-Token in H100 LLM Serving
quote: the regime where cache pressure erodes them
proves: Benchmark of prefix reuse vs TTFT on H100 including a cache-pressure regime and varied arrival patterns.
does_not_prove: Abstract reports steady-state regimes; no burst-recovery or hysteresis finding stated.
bearing: threatens C2 (characterizes pressure regime); scale evidence

title: Minima-KV: Retention-Preserving KV Cache Compression with Mixed-Format Paged Attention
quote: every live-request page remains addressable
proves: Mixed-format paged KV (FP8 recent/anchor pages, packed 3-bit older pages) in a serving page layout.
does_not_prove: Compression tiers are configuration-bound, not input-dependent; no open-loop load, admission, or workload-shift test on the abstract page.
bearing: adjacent to C1

title: CONCUR: High-Throughput Agentic Batch Inference of LLM via Congestion-Based Concurrency Control
quote: We identify this phenomenon as middle-phase thrashing, a previously under-characterized pathology
proves: Agentic batch inference enters a phase where memory is saturated but hit rate collapses ("vicious cycle of eviction and recomputation"); congestion-based feedback admission on KV usage and hit rate gives up to 4.09x; full text says hit rate "partially recover[s]" in cooldown.
does_not_prove: Offline batch only; no open-loop arrivals; no step-down test of whether the warm state returns at the same load (hysteresis).
bearing: threatens C2 (thrashing and its mitigation exist); bounds C2 to online hysteresis

title: Benchmarking LLM Serving Systems for Agentic AI Workloads with XPerf
quote: For the remaining applications, the hit rate drops sharply
proves: Real agent apps show a steady-state prefix-cache hit-rate cliff from thrashing as request rate rises; added load can reduce throughput because evicted prefixes are recomputed.
does_not_prove: Steady-state sweep only; no step-down or recovery test; no mitigation.
bearing: threatens C2 (thrashing cliff characterized); supports C2 relevance

title: Metronome: Bound the Cache, Keep the Beat for Real-Time Interaction Model Serving
quote: The collapse is metastable -- identical five-minute runs collapse or survive on run-to-run variance
proves: Real-engine metastable collapse when pinned, monotonically growing streaming-session KV exhausts the pool; fixed by bounding resident state.
does_not_prove: Mechanism is pinned session state, not prefix-cache eviction; no read-through refill dynamics.
bearing: threatens C2 (metastable KV collapse wording taken; different mechanism)

title: Metastability in Queues
quote: In certain parameter regimes, the system has two stable equilibria
proves: Fluid models with congestion-dependent service rate are bistable; gives the theory template (state-dependent service, two equilibria, transitions).
does_not_prove: No caches; no LLM-specific service function.
bearing: supports C2 (theory template); adjacent

title: A Queueing-Theoretic Framework for Stability Analysis of LLM Inference with KV Cache Memory Constraints
quote: the first queueing-theoretic framework that explicitly incorporates both computation and GPU memory constraints
proves: Stability analysis of LLM inference with compute and KV-memory constraints exists.
does_not_prove: Abstract does not model prefix caching or hit-rate-dependent service rate.
bearing: adjacent to C2 (model to extend)

title: [RFC]: Context-Aware KV-Cache Retention API (Prioritized Evictions) (vllm#37003)
quote: Agentic workloads break prefix caching under concurrent load.
proves: Upstream states agent blocks are evicted during tool-call pauses under concurrent load, causing full recompute; proposes retention priorities.
does_not_prove: No burst/recovery framing; design only.
bearing: supports C2 relevance; scoop risk on mitigation side

title: [Bug]Severe decode throughput collapse after KV cache retraction (~14x degradation) (sglang#26248)
quote: decode throughput collapses from ~429 tok/s to ~20-38 tok/s
proves: A user reports throughput collapse after a KV-pool-full retraction that does not recover.
does_not_prove: No controlled restoration of demand, no root cause; closed by inactivity bot, not fixed.
bearing: supports C2 relevance (persistent post-pressure degradation reported)

title: DEP: Request Admission and Rejection Controls (dynamo#9755)
quote: uncached-token limits protect prefill capacity
proves: Cache-aware admission and early rejection designed for Dynamo; a mandatory baseline.
does_not_prove: Does not show which gates shipped or whether they prevent persistence.
bearing: threatens C2 mitigation novelty; baseline

title: Metastable Failures in Distributed Systems (full text)
quote: the cache will still be filled, which steadily increases the hit rate until the system is healthy again
proves: Read-through caches self-heal when the fill completes even if the client gives up; look-aside caches can lock into the bad state.
does_not_prove: LLM prefix caches are read-through only if the prefill completes; a client abort mid-prefill may leave the cache unfilled (not addressed).
bearing: threatens C2 (self-healing argument); sharpens C2 (abort-before-fill turns read-through into look-aside)

title: Service-Induced Congestion in Memory-Constrained LLM Serving
quote: abstracting away system-specific recovery costs such as prefill recomputation, swapping, or prefix-cache reuse
proves: Ao, Dong, Luo, Simchi-Levi: fluid model of KV-constrained serving; the eviction-free equilibrium is unstable under standard admission and the system "does not return to eviction-free operation"; derives admission and request-mixing principles.
does_not_prove: Explicitly abstracts away prefill recomputation and prefix-cache reuse, so hit-rate-dependent service and cache capacity shrinking with in-flight KV are not modeled.
bearing: closest threat to C2; C2 extends its model with prefix reuse; scoop risk (same group as L249)

title: Sticky Until Saturated: Token-Aware Routing in llm-d
quote: the warm endpoint keeps absorbing load past the point where a cold endpoint would serve the request faster
proves: Cluster routing with prefix affinity settles into either a stable partition or eviction churn depending on one threshold; shipped saturation override.
does_not_prove: Cluster router level, not a single engine's pool; no recovery-time or hysteresis measurement.
bearing: supports C2 (bistability observed at cluster scale); scale arm

title: The KV Cache Working Set: Online Capacity Planning for LLM Inference Systems
quote: We present KVSET, an online analyzer that estimates the KV cache working set of LLM serving workloads.
proves: Steady-state capacity planning tool for prefix caches (the bigger-cache baseline has a sizing method).
does_not_prove: No bursts, transients, or recovery.
bearing: baseline for C2 (headroom sizing)
